output.brief: The buffering problem is not the new CDN. Session data for 12–25 October shows that only the smart-TV app version 5.2 has the problem: about 5.9% of viewing time stalled, on all three major ISPs. Every other client, including older TV app versions, the web player and the phone apps, is at 0.6–0.7% while also served by Tessaline. Before the switch, all clients were normal on Corvane. Version 5.2 went live on 9 October, the same day as the cutover, and that is why it looked like the CDN. The country-level dashboard can't show a breakdown by app version, so it hid this. The handball launch doesn't explain it either: match nights show no extra stalling. Don't approve Mireille's plan. A breach notice, withheld fees and a move back to Corvane would punish the wrong party and wouldn't fix the stalls. Muting the alert would also hide a live problem. Next: revert the 5.2 adaptive-streaming settings in Kestria, hold the wider rollout, and have the app team find the fault. Don't offer free months yet, because the 1 October price rise also plausibly drove cancellations. Add app version and device breakdowns to the dashboard and alerts. I'm fairly confident in the cause. The cancellation link is still unproven.
